Part b requires computing v(1) and a(1) and justifying with their signs, which targets the justification skill. Part c requires locating the zeros of v on [0,5] with the calculator and integrating |v|, a multi-step procedure. stimulus.description: A particle moves along the x-axis. Its velocity is v(t) = 3 sin((3/2)t) + 0.5 t - 1 for 0 ≤ t ≤ 5, where t is in seconds and v is in meters per second. The particle is at position x = 3 at time t = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the acceleration of the particle at time $t=1$. Include units of measure.
parts.model_answer: a(1) = v'(1) = 0.818 meters per second squared.

rubric_rows.criterion: Answer with units (differentiates v and evaluates; value correct)

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Is the speed of the particle increasing or decreasing at time $t=1$? Give a reason for your answer.
parts.model_answer: v(1) = 2.492 is positive and a(1) = 0.818 is positive; the signs are the same, so the speed is increasing.

rubric_rows.criterion: Determines the signs of velocity and acceleration at the given time
Concludes using the rule: same signs means speed increasing, opposite signs means decreasing (reason)

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the total distance traveled by the particle from time $t=0$ to $t=5$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Sets up the integral of the absolute value of velocity (|v|)
Evaluates with a calculator (value within tolerance)
Answer with units

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the position of the particle at time $t=5$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Uses the initial position plus the integral of velocity (net change)
Evaluates the integral with a calculator (net displacement)
Answer: the position

difficultyRationale: Standard AP FRQ-style implicit differentiation: derive dy/dx using product and chain rules, evaluate slope for tangent and normal lines, and find horizontal tangents by setting the numerator to zero, substituting into the curve, and checking that the denominator is nonzero. Multiple procedures are chained, but the numbers are clean and the scope is limited to first derivatives. Difficulty comes from legitimate conceptual sources.

stimulus.description: Consider the curve given by the equation x^2 + 1xy + 1y^2 = 3.

parts.label: a
parts.model_answer: Differentiating implicitly: 2x + 1(y + x dy/dx) + 2y dy/dx = 0, so dy/dx = -(2x + 1y)/(1x + 2y).

rubric_rows.criterion: Differentiates x^2 and the product xy correctly (product rule)
Differentiates the y^2 term with the chain rule
Isolates dy/dx to reach the stated expression

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write an equation for the line tangent to the curve at the point $(1,1)$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Slope at the point (answer)
Tangent line equation in point-slope form

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of every point on the curve at which the tangent line is horizontal.
parts.model_answer: Horizontal tangent when 2x + 1y = 0, i.e. y = -2x/1; the points are (-1, 2), (1, -2).

rubric_rows.criterion: Sets the numerator of dy/dx equal to zero (2x + 1y = 0)
Substitutes into the curve equation and finds the points (answer)

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Write an equation for the line normal to the curve at the point $(1,1)$. (The normal line is the line perpendicular to the tangent line at that point.)

rubric_rows.criterion: Normal slope is the negative reciprocal of the tangent slope (answer)
Equation of the normal line in point-slope form
